runs.text: ¶ Item, Modo de estar no Zaxiqui muita gẽ

lines.note: Continues hishito from f202: many people sitting closely in a zashiki. This actual opening confirms the preceding bottom-right Item as an anticipatory catchword.
Te completes gente, with apertada describing the crowded group. The crop contains the full short continuation, including its closing punctuation.

runs.text: Certo manjar q̃ ſe faz de grãos, trigo

lines.note: Hishio is a preparation of pulses, wheat, and salt. The small first stroke of trigo is supported by the scan and the ingredient list, correcting OCR's rigo.
The ingredients are thoroughly pounded and ground. Fo- starts hone, bones, in the metaphorical example that follows.
Hone wo hishio ni seraruru tomo imagines one's bones being reduced to paste. Christãouo is the Christian identity in the Japanese sentence, not a switch to a Portuguese explanatory clause.
Kayuru koto arumai denies changing that identity. The concessive Portuguese begins even if they grind me; do not replace the historical kayuru with a modern verb form.

runs.text: os oſſos, & desfação não eide deixar de ſer

lines.note: The bones may be ground and destroyed, but the speaker will not cease to be Christian. Eide is retained as printed, and the s forms are not regularized from modern spelling.
Christão completes the declared identity. This italic word belongs to the Portuguese translation, unlike the upright borrowed term in the Japanese example.
A homonymous hishio denotes an ebbing or low tide. The maritime gloss distinguishes it entirely from the food above.
Hishio ni naru means the tide ebbing. The repeated accented marè is preserved without modernization.

runs.text: Cana, ou grelo da erua que ſe cha

lines.note: Hishizzuru is the stem or shoot of the hishi plant. The compound's second part corresponds to a plant stem, not a verb in suru.
Fixi supplies the named plant inside Portuguese prose and is upright. This short continuation is still part of the hishizzuru definition.

runs.text: Eſcritura, ou liuro de ſegredos. ¶ Itẽ,

lines.note: Hisho is a secret writing or book. Escritura here means writing or document, not necessarily Christian Scripture.
The entry adds secrecy itself and mono wo hisho suru, concealing something. The Japanese example agrees with the following Portuguese infinitive.
Der completes esconder, and algũa couſa supplies its object. Keep the physical line division and nasal abbreviation.
Hishoo is kanashimi itamu, grieving painfully. The Portuguese describes sorrowful suffering rather than the secret-document sense of unaccented hisho.
The grief is further glossed affligir-se. Two f stems are visible in the ligature cluster, supporting affligirſe rather than OCR's single-f form.
Hishuu is kanashimi ureo(o), sorrow or grieving. The long-u headword and the following Portuguese noun/verb alternatives are coherent.
Tristecerſe completes entristecer-se. It is a continuation of the verb, not another independent entry.
Hissha is a fude-tori, a scribe. The scan separates the explanatory i, from Fixxa; OCR had attached and misplaced it.
Hissei is fude no ikioi, the force or character of brushwork. The Portuguese covers handwriting and painting rather than simply the writer's social role.

runs.text: ou pintura em que ſe hum eſmerou. ¶

lines.note: The writing or painting is executed with care or mastery. The example repeats hissei, split after Fix-.
Hissei wo tsukusu means exerting one's skill in writing or painting. The long s in tçucuſu remains the OCR reading because it matches the visible form.
Pintar completes the alternative artistic activity. This short row closes the same expression.
Hisshi is kanarazu shi suru, certain death. The gloss is not the common modern adverbial sense of desperate effort.
Death is unavoidable, certain, and determined. These qualifications reinforce the literal interpretation of the Japanese compound.
Another hisshi is fude and kami, brush and paper. The identical sound represents a different compound from certain death.
Hisshi ni tsukushigatashi means that writing cannot exhaust the matter. A conspicuous paragraph mark before the example was omitted by OCR and is restored.

runs.text: de acabar de eſcreuer, ou explicar por pena.

lines.note: The Portuguese spells out inability to finish writing or explaining with a pen. It confirms the idiomatic reading rather than physical shortage of paper.
Hisshime, hisshimuru, hisshimeta means tightening strongly. The next row supplies binding implements.
Rope or cord exemplifies how the tightening is done. Cordão remains accented on the printed vowel rather than standardized from neighbouring instances.

runs.text: Pelle que trazem os ſoldados pera ſe

lines.note: Hisshiki is a skin carried by soldiers for sitting. The gloss describes a portable seating hide, with additional users below.

runs.text: aßentarem, ou de que vſão outras peßoas pera

lines.note: Other people also use the hide as a seat. The two ß forms retain the ligature convention; the text does not restrict this object exclusively to soldiers.
Se assentar completes the sitting purpose. It closes the hide entry rather than introducing a separate verb.

runs.text: Adu. Modo de fazer algũa cou-

lines.note: Hisshito is an adverb describing how something is done. Its doubled x records the stronger consonant form compared with hishito on f202.

runs.text: ſa com efficacia, ou rijamente, ou modo de

lines.note: The action is effective or forceful; the definition then turns to closeness. Efficacia is the source's spelling, without an added modern accent.

runs.text: eſtar a couſa junta, & apertada. Vt,

lines.note: The object can also be closely joined or pressed together. Vt introduces the divided hisshito example and is italic in the scan.
Hisshito utsu or yamasuru concerns hard blows. Retain the less familiar yamasuru, whose printed letters are clear, rather than invent a more familiar Japanese verb.
Jamente completes rijamente, forcefully. No new hyphen is supplied to the previous ri merely because the word crosses a row.
Hiya is a fire-arrow, with rocket added as another sense. This is not the cold-related hiya family that begins below.
Hiya wo iru is shooting a fire-arrow. The scan has uo, agreeing with the object of iru, and corrects OCR's no.

runs.text: ou com foguete pegado na frecha.

lines.note: The alternative is a rocket attached to the arrow. The gloss thus specifies the projectile construction instead of a wholly unrelated meaning of fire.
Hiyaku is a highly valued medicine, treated almost as a secret. This fits the secret-remedy compound rather than a flying or jumping verb.

runs.text: eſcondida que logo obra. ¶ Item, Aliquã

lines.note: The medicine works promptly. Aliquã begins Latin aliquando, sometimes, introducing a contrasting usage on the next row.

runs.text: do, Mezinha leue, & de pouca ſustancia.

lines.note: Sometimes it means a mild medicine of little substance. The apparent contrast is explicitly marked by aliquando and should not be harmonized away.
Hiyai is cold or being cold, marked as Ximo usage. The damaged capital belongs to the word; X. is a separate upright regional label.
Hiyasa is the associated noun, coldness. Its indented isolated row is part of the adjective's entry, not a running label.
Hiyoo is the associated adverbial form. It sits beneath hiyasa within the column; unlike a bottom-right next-page catchword, it belongs in the body.
Hiyamugi is cold wheat noodles. Portuguese aletria is the comparison used for the noodle form, not a reason to replace the Japanese name with a European dish.
The noodles are eaten in that cold, fresh state. Aßi retains the ligature transcription and completes the manner of serving.
Hiyake is scorching or drying in drought. The scan joins Oqueimarſe; OCR's internal break in queimar is removed without imposing modern spacing on the initial article.

runs.text: ou muito ſol, como os campos, & varzeas.

lines.note: Strong sun dries fields and lowland cultivated plots. This completes the agricultural sense before the bodily sunburn sense below.

runs.text: ¶ Item, Abraſarſe, ou queimarſe ao ſol

lines.note: The entry additionally describes scorching or burning in sunlight. The reflexive Portuguese concerns the affected body, not deliberate setting of fire.
The body or face is sunburned; hiyake ga suru gives the Japanese construction. The particle ga agrees with that intransitive event.
Idem explicitly equates the example with the sunburn definition. The short isolated row is not furniture.
Hiyaketa denotes dry-field plots. Portuguese de sequeiro distinguishes land lacking irrigation; retain the printed voiced da rather than modernize the compound.
Hiyashi, hiyasu, hiya(i)ta is cooling something. The historical -aita past is compatible with the dictionary's s-verb onbin and is not automatically hiyashita.

runs.text: tendoa na agoa. O eſfriar ao vento he,

lines.note: Immersion in water is contrasted with cooling in wind. He, not OCR's be, is the copula; Caza- begins the Japanese alternative and is visibly upright.
Same completes kazasame, kazasamuru. Its first glyph is long s, not f; the first fragment is actually italic while uru is upright, an irregular typeface boundary preserved from the scan.
Hiyashimono is cold food that refreshes. This is a general class before the more specific noodle sense on the next row.

runs.text: refreſca. X. ¶ Item, Aletria cozida fria.

lines.note: The regional label X. closes the first sense. A second sense is cooked noodles served cold; the label is upright while the surrounding prose is italic.

runs.text: Certo Xiru frio com algũa miſtura

lines.note: Hiyashiru is a cold shiru with an admixture. Xiru is an embedded Japanese food term and appears italic, which should not be overridden by its usual upright treatment elsewhere.

runs.text: de eruas que ſe come no verão.

lines.note: Herbs are mixed into the dish, which is eaten in summer. The season reinforces the cold-serving interpretation.
Hiyayakana describes something cold and fresh. The printed adjective is retained rather than replaced with a modern preferred spelling.
Hiyazake is cold sake, rendered vinho frio. The European beverage category is the dictionary's gloss, not a botanical claim about grapes.
Hiye, hiyuru, hiyeta is becoming cold or feeling cold. It is intransitive, in contrast to hiyasu above.
Hiye also denotes an illness associated with cold. Hiye wo waz- introduces the example, with the word divided between the two z characters.
Wazzuroo completes falling ill from cold. X. is an upright regional marker, not a Japanese syllable or part of adoecer.

runs.text: Hum legume, ou ſemente de cor preta

lines.note: Another hie is a dark-coloured grain or seed. This is the cereal name, unrelated to the preceding illness apart from pronunciation.
Como milho compares the grain with millet-like cereal. The brief comparison does not establish a modern botanical species by itself.

runs.text: Carnegão de eſpinha do roſto que ſe pa-

lines.note: Hie also names the core of a facial spot. Carnegão and espinha belong to that bodily description, not the cereal definition itself.

runs.text: rece com eſta ſemente. ¶ Item, Ameſma

lines.note: The core resembles the previously named seed. The entry then adds the spot itself as a further sense.
Espinha do rosto completes the whole-spot sense. This is a semantic extension from the seed-like core, not another isolated headword.
Hiyegai is corrected by the dictionary itself to hiye no kai, a gruel. Meliùs is Latin better, and must not be included in the Japanese reading.
The gruel is made from that dark millet-like grain. The demonstrative links it back to hie, not to cold rice in the following entry.
Hiyeii is cold cooked rice. The iy ending is the dictionary's way of keeping the rice word's vowel sequence, not a ji sound.
Hiyemono is something naturally cooling. The gloss begins an example involving food rather than merely an object chilled externally.
Such food cools the stomach. Eſtamago is visibly printed with a; retain it despite modern estômago and do not use dictionary familiarity to normalize the vowel.

Hiyet, opening and reading a letter, is glossed hiraqi miru. Enlarging the worn gap after Ab reveals a small lower-stroke remnant compatible with r; Abrĩdo is inferred from this and the clear Abrindo in the next line. This is a damaged reading, not a fully legible r.
Gojo hiyet seshime sooro is a formal letter-reading expression. The weak final o of Gojo is not supplied with an accent merely because gojoo is expected.
The translation says that on opening the addressee's letter the speaker read or saw it. Ali is a li, I read it, rather than the locative ali in this context.
Hiyoo is expenditure: tsuyashi mochijru, with zoosa as an equivalent. The circumflex in the headword is preserved and not confused with the open-o mark in Zoosa.
Hiyoo ga iru means there is expense or something costs money. The repeated accented headword agrees with the cost sense.
E custo completes the paired Portuguese gloss. It remains a body continuation despite its brevity.
Another hiyoo is keeping something hidden for use. Cacuxi mochijru and the Portuguese secret and valued distinguish this from expense.

Hiyoo no hoo exemplifies a secret law or teaching. Enlargement reveals a distinct shallow v above the final o, supporting fǒ rather than OCR's unaccented fo; this contrasts with the circumflex earlier in Fiyôno.
Deſtima means de estima, of esteem or value. Its joined spelling is preserved rather than split editorially.
Hiyoko is a chick or young chicken. The two Portuguese bird-age terms agree with the straightforward Japanese reading.
Hiyoku is explained as birds setting their wings alongside each other. This introduces the literary paired-bird image, not ordinary ornithological classification.

runs.text: paſſaros que voam com hũa aſa ſoo que tem

lines.note: Each bird has only one wing. The scan supports the separate long-s pair retained in paſſaros; no ligature normalization is imposed during this semantic review.

runs.text: ajudandoſe da do companheiro. Vſaſe em cõ-

lines.note: Each uses the companion's wing. The dictionary then says the expression is used comparatively, explicitly identifying the metaphorical extension.

runs.text: paração dos que muito ſe amão, & não po-

lines.note: The comparison concerns people who love one another intensely and cannot part. This matches the literary hiyoku image of inseparability.
Hiyoku no tori restates the paired-bird expression. Idem refers to the preceding description and comparison.
Hiyodori is compared with a starling. Preserve that historical gloss rather than substitute the modern bulbul identification into Level 1.
Hiyodorijoogo is a climbing plant name. The scan supports y in Fiyodori, not OCR's j; the compound and preceding bird name independently flag the mistake.
